# Longitudinal data of mixed type

##

library("clustGLMM")
data(students, package = "clustGLMM")
n <- length(unique(students$i))
```

```

# Model Overview

## 5 different outcome types

numeric, count, binary, ordinal and general categorical: 
$r\in\mathcal{R} = \mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Num}} \cup \mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Poi}} \cup \mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Bin}} \cup \mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Ord}} \cup \mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Cat}}$

\vspace*{-0.1cm}
$$
\eta_{ijr}^{(g)} = \mathbf{F}_{ijr}^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}_r^F + \mathbf{X}_{ijr}^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}_r^{(g)} + \mathbf{Z}_{ijr}^\top \mathbf{b}_{ir}
$$
\vspace*{-0.1cm}
\begin{align*}
  \left. Y_{ij}^r \,\right\vert\, U_i = g, \mathbf{b}_i^r, \mathbf{F}_{ijr}, \mathbf{X}_{ijr}, \mathbf{Z}_{ijr} 
  &\sim 
  \mathsf{N}\left(\eta_{ijr}^{(g)}, \; \left(\tau_r^{(g)}\right)^{-1}\right) 
  &\qquad r \in\mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Num}}
  \\
  \left. Y_{ij}^r \,\right\vert\, U_i = g, \mathbf{b}_i^r, \mathbf{F}_{ijr}, \mathbf{X}_{ijr}, \mathbf{Z}_{ijr} 
  &\sim 
  \mathsf{Pois}\left(\exp\left\{\eta_{ijr}^{(g)}\right\}\right) 
  &\qquad r \in\mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Poi}}
  \\
  \mathsf{P} \left[\left. Y_{ij}^r = 1 \,\right\vert\, U_i = g, \mathbf{b}_i^r, \mathbf{F}_{ijr}, \mathbf{X}_{ijr}, \mathbf{Z}_{ijr} \right] 
  &= 
  \mathsf{logit}^{-1} \left(\eta_{ijr}^{(g)}\right) 
  &\qquad r \in\mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Bin}}
  \\
  \mathsf{P} \left[\left. Y_{ij}^r > k \,\right\vert\, U_i = g, \mathbf{b}_i^r, \mathbf{F}_{ijr}, \mathbf{X}_{ijr}, \mathbf{Z}_{ijr} \right] 
  &= 
  \mathsf{logit}^{-1} \left(\eta_{ijr}^{(g)} - c_{k,r}^{(g)}\right) 
  &\qquad k = 0, 1, \ldots, K^r-1, \;r \in\mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Ord}}
  \\
  \mathsf{P} \left[\left. Y_{ij}^r = k \,\right\vert\, U_i = g, \mathbf{b}_i^r, \mathbf{F}_{ijr}, \mathbf{X}_{ijr}, \mathbf{Z}_{ijr} \right] 
  &= 
  \frac{\exp \eta_{ijkr}^{(g)}}{1 + \sum\limits_{\kappa=1}^{K^r-1} \exp \eta_{ij\kappa r}^{(g)}} 
  &\qquad k = 0, 1, \ldots, K^r-1, \;r \in\mathcal{R}^{\mathsf{Cat}}
\end{align*}

## Latent data - random effects, cluster allocations, missing outcome values

combined vector of random effects $\mathbf{b}_{i} = \left\{\mathbf{b}_i^r, r\in\mathcal{R}\right\} \,\vert\, U_i = g \,\sim\, \mathsf{N}_{d^R}\left(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{(g)}\right)$,
where $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{(g)} > 0$

cluster allocations $U_i \in \{1,\ldots, G\}$: $\mathsf{P}(U_i = g) = w_g$ for $g = 1, \ldots, G$

$$
  p(\mathbb{Y}_i \,\vert\, \mathbb{F}_{i}, \mathbb{X}_{i}, \mathbb{Z}_{i})
  = \sum\limits_{g=1}^{G} 
  w_g \int 
  p\left(\mathbb{Y}_i \,\left\vert\, U_i = g, \mathbf{b}_i;\, \boldsymbol{\beta}^F, \boldsymbol{\beta}^{(g)}, \boldsymbol{\tau}^{(g)}, \mathbf{c}^{(g)}, \mathbb{F}_{i}, \mathbb{X}_{i}, \mathbb{Z}_{i} \right.\right)
  p\left(\mathbf{b}_i \,\left\vert\, U_i = g;\, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{(g)}\right.\right)
  \mathrm{d} \mathbf{b}_i
$$

Moreover, outcome values $Y_{ij}^r$ _missing at random_ become model parameter.

## Bayesian inference via MCMC

uninformative prior distributions: normal ($\boldsymbol{\beta}^F, \boldsymbol{\beta}^{(g)}$), gamma ($\boldsymbol{\tau}^{(g)}$), Inverse Wishart ($\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{(g)}$)

sparse finite mixture prior for $\mathbf{w}$
$$
\boldsymbol{\theta} = \left\{\mathbb{Y}^{\mathsf{mis}}, \mathbf{U}, \mathbf{b}, \mathbf{w}, \boldsymbol{\beta}^F, \boldsymbol{\beta}^{(g)}, \boldsymbol{\tau}^{(g)}, \mathbf{c}^{(g)}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{(g)}, g = 1, \ldots, G \right\}
$$
$$
p(\boldsymbol{\theta} \, | \, \mathbb{Y}^{\mathsf{obs}}, \mathbb{F}, \mathbb{X}, \mathbb{Z}) 
\propto 
p(\mathbb{Y}^{\mathsf{obs}} \, | \, \boldsymbol{\theta}, \mathbb{F}, \mathbb{X}, \mathbb{Z}) 
\, 
p(\boldsymbol{\theta} \, | \, \mathbb{F}, \mathbb{X}, \mathbb{Z})
$$
Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampling algorithm (sampling in sub blocks $\boldsymbol{\omega} \subset \boldsymbol{\theta}$)

Metropolis proposal distribution based on Laplace approximation
$$
\ell (\boldsymbol{\omega}) := \log p (\boldsymbol{\omega} | \cdots) 
\approx 
\mathrm{const.} - 
\frac{1}{2} \left(\boldsymbol{\omega}-\widehat{\boldsymbol{\omega}}\right)^\top
\left[- \left.\frac{\partial^2 \ell(\boldsymbol{\omega})}{\partial \boldsymbol{\omega} \partial \boldsymbol{\omega}^\top }\right|_{\boldsymbol{\omega}=\widehat{\boldsymbol{\omega}}} \right]
\left(\boldsymbol{\omega}-\widehat{\boldsymbol{\omega}}\right)
$$
$$
\boldsymbol{\omega}^{\mathrm{proposal}} = \boldsymbol{\omega}^{\mathrm{current}} + \mathbf{s}, 
\qquad \text{where} \quad 
\mathbf{s} \sim 
\mathsf{N}_d\left(\mathbf{0}, c_{\boldsymbol{\omega}} \left[- \left.\frac{\partial^2 \ell(\boldsymbol{\omega})}{\partial \boldsymbol{\omega} \partial \boldsymbol{\omega}^\top }\right|_{\boldsymbol{\omega}=\widehat{\boldsymbol{\omega}}} \right]^{-1}\right)
$$
Proposal accepted with probability \quad
$\min\left\{1, \, \exp(\ell(\boldsymbol{\omega}^{\mathrm{proposal}}) -\ell(\boldsymbol{\omega}^{\mathrm{current}}))\right\}$

## Preparations for clustGLMM

```{r students-NAs, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
set.seed(31415)
nmis <- 6
na_indices <- na_true_vals <- list()
for (y in c("income", "ntrips", "satisfaction")) {
  na_indices[[y]] <- sort(sample(seq_len(nrow(students)), nmis))
  na_true_vals[[y]] <- students[na_indices[[y]], y]
  is.na(students[na_indices[[y]], y]) <- TRUE
}
```

Specification of outcome types

```{r students-family, echo=TRUE}
family <- c("num", "poi", "ord") # is also equivalent to
family <- c("gaussian", "poisson", "cumulative")
names(family) <- Ys <- c("income", "ntrips", "satisfaction")
```

`clustGLMM()` checks the required format, orders by type

## Formulas for linear predictor

```{r students-formula, echo=TRUE}
library("splines")
degree <- 2
knots <- c(18, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40)
inner <- knots[-c(1, length(knots))]
bound <- knots[c(1, length(knots))]
id <- "i"
formula <- list()
for (y in Ys) {
  formula[[y]] <- list()
  formula[[y]]$fixed <- ~ 1 # will become ~ 0
  formula[[y]]$group <- ~ bs(age, 
                             knots = inner, Boundary.knots = bound, 
                             degree = degree, intercept = FALSE)
  formula[[y]]$random <- ~ 1
  formula[[y]]$offset <- ""
}
```

## Adjusting algorithm settings

Which parameters should be group-specific?
```{r students-defaults, echo = TRUE}
(varying <- default_varying())
varying["prec_num"] <- FALSE   # change tau to common to all groups
```

Which parameters should be saved?
```{r students-defaults-2, echo = TRUE}
save <- default_save()
save["naY"] <- TRUE            # save estimates for missing Y values
```

```{r students-defaults-other, echo = TRUE, eval = F}
default_param()        # hyperparameters for prior distributions
default_tuning()       # algorithm tuning parameters + other settings
```

## The basic use of clustGLMM()

```{r students-mcmc-initial, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE, results=FALSE}
set.seed(12345678)
mcmc <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = id, family = family, data = students,
                  G = 10, nchains = 2, iter = 3000, 
                  varying = varying, save = save,
                  standardize = TRUE)
```

```{r clustGLMM-auxiliary-print, echo = F}
cat("Chain: 1, (100 %)\nChain: 2, (100 %)")
```
```{r saving-students-mcmc-initial, eval = F, echo = F}
save(mcmc, file = file.path(WD, "data", "students_mcmc_initial.RData"))
```

```{r loading-students-mcmc-initial, eval = T, echo = F}
load(file.path(WD, "data", "students_mcmc_initial.RData"))
```

##

```{r students-mcmc-initial-plot, echo=TRUE, out.height = "85%"}
plot(mcmc, ng_trace_chain_split = FALSE)
```

## Continue in sampling

```{r students-mcmc, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE, results=FALSE}
set.seed(1234)
mcmc <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = id, family = family, data = students,
                  inits = mcmc$last,                # last -> initial values
                  G = 10, nchains = 2, iter = 1000, 
                  varying = varying, save = save,
                  standardize = TRUE)
```

```{r clustGLMM-auxiliary-print2, echo = F}

students[, paste0("Uclustering", 1)] <- mcmc_pp$clustering[students$i, 1]
# confusion matrix
table(students[students$j == 1, c("g", paste0("Uclustering", 1))])
```

## Prediction of missing values

\vspace*{-0.3cm}
```{r students-mcmc-naY, echo = FALSE, out.height = "85%"}
par(mar = c(4, 4, 0.5, 0.5), mfrow = nice_nrow_ncol(nmis))
y <- "income"
for (j in 1:nmis) {
  plot_kerneldensity(mcmc_pp, what = "naY", yspec = y, dimspec = j, labcex = 0.8)
  # true value
  abline(v = as.numeric(na_true_vals[[y]][j]), col = "seagreen", lty = 2)
  # 95% CI
  abline(v = sum_pp$coda_summary[[1]]$quantiles[paste0("naY_",y,"[",j,"]"),
                                                c("2.5%","97.5%")], 
         col = "black", lty = 3)
}
```

## 

```{r students-predict-income-and-ntrips-code, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
age_grid <- seq(18, 40, by = 0.1)
newdata <- data.frame(age = age_grid)
burnin <- 0
thin <- 1
ch <- 1
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 0.5))
for (y in c(mcmc_pp$Nums, mcmc_pp$Pois)) {
  ...
  pred <- predict(mcmc_pp, newdata, y = y, type = "response", method = "samples",
                  burnin = burnin, thin = thin, chain = ch)
  ...
  ## Posterior predictive distribution for each cluster separately
  pred <- predict(mcmc_pp, newdata, y = y, 
                  type = "posterior_predictive_response",
                  posterior_predictive_by_cluster = TRUE,
                  method = "samples",
                  burnin = burnin, thin = thin, chain = ch)
  ...
}
```

## 

```{r students-predict-income-and-ntrips-plot, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, out.height = "95%"}
age_grid <- seq(18, 40, by = 0.1)
newdata <- data.frame(age = age_grid)
  
burnin <- 0
thin <- 1
ch <- 1
COL <- colorspace::rainbow_hcl(mcmc_pp$modeGplus[ch], c = 80, l = 50)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 0.5))
for (y in c(mcmc_pp$Nums, mcmc_pp$Pois)) {
  plot_num_vs_x_grouped(students, y = y, x = "age", g = paste0("Uclustering", ch), id = id, 
                        legend_placement = "topleft", add_lowess = FALSE)
  
  pred <- predict(mcmc_pp, newdata, y = y, type = "response", method = "samples",
                  burnin = burnin, thin = thin, chain = ch)
  
  for (g in mcmc_pp$clusters[[ch]]) {
    lines(x = age_grid, y = pred$fit[, paste0("(", g, ")")], col = COL[g], lwd = 3)
    lines(x = age_grid, y = pred$lwr[, paste0("(", g, ")")], col = COL[g], lty = 2)
    lines(x = age_grid, y = pred$upr[, paste0("(", g, ")")], col = COL[g], lty = 2)
  }
  
  ## Posterior predictive distribution for each cluster separately
  pred <- predict(mcmc_pp, newdata, y = y, 
                  type = "posterior_predictive_response",
                  posterior_predictive_by_cluster = TRUE,
                  method = "samples",
                  burnin = burnin, thin = thin, chain = ch)
  for (g in mcmc_pp$clusters[[ch]]) {
    lines(x = age_grid, y = pred$lwr[, g], col = COL[g], lty = 1)
    lines(x = age_grid, y = pred$upr[, g], col = COL[g], lty = 1)
  }
}
```

##

```{r students-predict-satisfaction, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, out.height = "95%"}
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
for (y in mcmc_pp$Ords) {
  # Predicted spline curves 
  maxK <- mcmc_pp$Kord[y]
  pred <- predict(mcmc_pp, newdata, y = y, type = "link", 
                  what = "fg", method = "samples", 
                  burnin = burnin, thin = thin, chain = ch)
  
  par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 0.5))
  plot(x = 0, y = 0, type = "n",
       xlim = range(age_grid), ylim = range(unlist(pred)),
       xlab = "age", ylab = "Linear predictor - ordered intercept",
       main = y)
  for (k in 1:maxK) {
    for (g in mcmc_pp$clusters[[ch]]) {
      lines(x = age_grid, y = pred$fit[, paste0("(", g, ")"), paste0("k=", k)],
            col = COL[g], lwd = 3)
      lines(x = age_grid, y = pred$lwr[, paste0("(", g, ")"), paste0("k=", k)],
            col = COL[g], lty = 2)
      lines(x = age_grid, y = pred$upr[, paste0("(", g, ")"), paste0("k=", k)],
            col = COL[g], lty = 2)
    }
  }
  
  # Predicted probabilities
  pred <- predict(mcmc_pp, newdata, y = y, type = "response", 
                  what = "fg", method = "samples", 
                  burnin = burnin, thin = thin, chain = ch)
  
  par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 2.5))
  plot(x = 0, y = 0, type = "n",
       xlim = range(age_grid), ylim = range(1, maxK+2),
       xlab = "age", ylab = "Predicted probability for level k",
       yaxt = "n",
       main = y)
  axis(2, at = 0.5+1:(maxK+1), labels = paste0("k=", 0:maxK))
  for (p in c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)) {
    axis(4, at = p+1:(maxK+1), labels = rep(p, maxK+1), las = 1, cex = 0.8)
  }
  for (k in 1:(maxK+1)) {
    for (g in mcmc_pp$clusters[[ch]]) {
      lines(x = age_grid, y = k+pred$fit[, paste0("(", g, ")"), paste0("k=", k)],
            col = COL[g], lwd = 3)
      lines(x = age_grid, y = k+pred$lwr[, paste0("(", g, ")"), paste0("k=", k)],
            col = COL[g], lty = 2)
      lines(x = age_grid, y = k+pred$upr[, paste0("(", g, ")"), paste0("k=", k)],
            col = COL[g], lty = 2)
    }
  }
  
  # Spineplots
  par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 0.5))
    plot_cat_vs_x_grouped(students, y = y, x = "age",
                          group = paste0("Uclustering", ch), main = y)
}
```
